subject.title: Unhandled Playwright assertion error in CRSession._onMessage crashes Gateway

question: Should OpenClaw handle this CRSession CDP assertion with a narrow classifier/profile reconnect path, or should browser/CDP control move behind a stronger isolation boundary such as a subprocess or extension bridge?
rationale: Source inspection shows the current fatal path, but the durable fix changes how much unknown Playwright state the main Gateway should suppress versus isolate, which is a product and reliability boundary decision.

options.title: Design browser recovery boundary first
options.body: Keep this issue open while a browser/Gateway owner specifies recovery semantics, proof requirements, and whether the affected profile should be quarantined, reconnected, or isolated out of process.

options.title: Accept a narrow CRSession classifier
options.body: Treat only well-identified Playwright CRSession assertion shapes as non-fatal and reconnect the affected browser profile while preserving the existing fatal behavior for unknown rejections.

options.title: Wait for live repro before choosing code
options.body: Require a fresh current-main CRSession CDP reproduction before choosing either classifier or isolation work.

recommendation.title: Design browser recovery boundary first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while a browser/Gateway owner specifies recovery semantics, proof requirements, and whether the affected profile should be quarantined, reconnected, or isolated out of process.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current-main history across the browser/CDP policy path and the process-level unhandled-rejection surface.
